newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Western firms said keen on Abu Dhabi Free Zone.
newsitem.headline: Western firms said keen on Abu Dhabi Free Zone.

text.p: Several international companies were seeking to invest in the new Abu Dhabi Free Zone, its director general said on Monday.
"Several international companies are interested in investing in the Free Zone," Mohammed al-Hosani told Reuters on the sidelines of an investment and industrial development conference in Abu Dhabi.
"These are companies from several sectors including finance, insurance and shipping," he said. Hosani declined to name the companies, but said they were major Western firms.

The United Arab Emirates is trying to diversify its economy and find more channels for foreign and private investment. Abu Dhabi has been blessed with vast oil wealth, but bankers say its economy will not mature without diversification and privatisation.
Hosani said the infrastructure work on the free zone would cost $3.0 billion, but he would not provide details of the expected total foreign investment in the project.
"We have not decided how much of a share foreign investors would have," he said.
An initial public offering would be held in the second half of 1997, Hosani said.
Asked whether the UAE's offset programme would be involved in the free zone scheme, he said: "Offset is interested in being involved."

Major Western arms manufacturers have expressed frustration with the offset programme -- implemented by the UAE as part of its bid to diversify its oil-driven economy -- saying there were not enough investment opportunities in the UAE.

Industry sources said the free zone would provide a key investment opportunity if it succeeds. But Western diplomats say the Abu Dhabi zone would face stiff competition from neighbouring Dubai's Jebel Ali Free Zone.
Abu Dhabi Free Zone officials have said it was not intended to compete with Jebel Ali.
The free zone in Abu Dhabi, the richest of the seven states in the UAE, will include storage facilities, a new port, airport and commodities trading exchanges.
The first stage of the zone will be built on the island of Saadiyat, just east of Abu Dhabi city, and will specialise in the storage, transporation and trading of 67 commodities.
The free zone authority has said it would take between three and four years to complete the project.
Industry sources said they expected construction of the project to start in about two years.
